- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price increases, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” penalty: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day after peak for 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility bias — suppress forecast variance and favor mean-reversion paths toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-term downward corrections; apply a “tail correction” by reducing final 5–7 days of forecast by 1–3% if true outcome shows sustained decline.
- If true outcome deviates >3% from 7-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, even if sentiment remains unchanged — model is overconfident in static sentiment signals.
